mainTopic: A condemned animal's calf, general warnings for the death penalty, and the wording of the mixed-group case of נסקלין and נשרפין
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about a cow sentenced to death and whether her calf is forbidden. The גמרא asks how the ברייתא fits the view that 'זה וזה גורם' is permitted. רבינא answers that the forbidden calf was already inside its mother when her verdict was finalized, because 'עובר ירך אמו'. The גמרא then turns to the משנה of 'כל חייבי מיתות' and tries to prove that a warning for a harsher death counts for a lighter one. רבי ירמיה rejects the proof: the case is one where the warning was general (סתם). That fits the תנא קמא, who learns from the מקושש, and not רבי יהודה, who calls the מקושש a one-time ruling. Next, רב יחזקאל and his son רב יהודה argue over the wording of the משנה about נסקלין mixed with נשרפין, using the rule of following the majority. רב יהודה explains that the חכמים's line 'סקילה is harsher' is only a reply to רבי שמעון. The amud ends as שמואל starts to respond to רב יהודה, and his words continue on the next amud.

steps.title: A problem for the view that two combined causes are permitted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the ברייתא about the condemned cow's calf can be explained according to the view that 'זה וזה גורם' is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says that when a permitted thing and a forbidden thing together cause a result, the result is permitted, what can we say?
steps.whatsHappening: The earlier explanation of the ברייתא only worked for the view that 'זה וזה גורם' is forbidden. Now the גמרא asks how the view that it is permitted would explain the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A calf comes from two sources: the father bull, which is permitted, and the condemned mother, which is forbidden. According to the view that 'זה וזה גורם מותר', such a calf should be permitted. So the ברייתא's ruling that the calf is forbidden does not fit this view as it was explained so far.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This and that cause': a result produced by both a permitted and a forbidden source together
Permitted
What is there to say? (a challenge formula)

phrases.english: But according to the one who says:
'this and that cause' – it is permitted,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the permitted bull and 'that' is the forbidden condemned cow. Both caused the calf.

phrases.english: what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר זֶה וָזֶה גּוֹרֵם מוּתָּר מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier explanation of the ברייתא, which only fit the view that 'זה וזה גורם אסור'.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the ברייתא's forbidden calf was conceived after the verdict
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'זה וזה גורם מותר', a calf conceived after the verdict comes partly from a permitted bull and should be permitted, so the ברייתא's ruling stays unexplained.

steps.title: רבינא rereads the case: the fetus is part of its mother
steps.stepSummary: רבינא changes the reading of the ברייתא. The forbidden case is a cow that became pregnant before her verdict and gave birth after it, because a fetus counts as part of its mother's body.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבינא said: Say it this way. If before her verdict was finalized she both conceived and gave birth, her calf is permitted. If before her verdict was finalized she conceived, but she gave birth after the verdict was finalized, her calf is forbidden. A fetus is like its mother's thigh.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the problem by reading the ברייתא differently, so that it works even for the view that 'זה וזה גורם מותר'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The forbidden case is no longer about a calf conceived after the verdict. It is about a calf that was inside the mother when she was sentenced. Since 'עובר ירך אמו', the fetus was part of the condemned cow at the moment of the verdict, so the bull's role does not matter and the calf is forbidden according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Say (read the text this way): a signal that the wording is being adjusted
Her verdict was finalized
She conceived and gave birth
A fetus is like its mother's thigh, meaning it is part of her body

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבינא, a calf is forbidden only if it was inside the cow when her verdict was finalized, because a fetus is part of its mother.
steps.confusionAlert: The ruling does not depend on when the calf was born. It depends on whether the calf was already inside the mother at the moment of the verdict.
steps.whyThisMatters: The principle 'עובר ירך אמו' comes up in many places in ש"ס. Here it lets the ברייתא work for both sides of the 'זה וזה גורם' debate.

phrases.english: Rather, Ravina said: say,
phrases.notes: 'Say' means: read the ברייתא this way instead of how we read it before.

phrases.english: if before her verdict was finalized
she conceived and gave birth – her offspring is permitted,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִגְמַר דִּינָה עִיבְּרָה
phrases.english: and if before her verdict was finalized she conceived
and after her verdict was finalized she gave birth –
her offspring is forbidden.
A fetus is its mother's thigh.
phrases.notes: He means the unborn calf counts as a limb of the mother, so it shares her condemned status.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1 by redefining the case in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text and redefining the case (אימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The forbidden calf was conceived after the verdict, so it depends on 'זה וזה גורם'.
steps.terutzMaskana: The forbidden calf was already a fetus at the time of the verdict, and since 'עובר ירך אמו' it is forbidden according to everyone.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה: a warning for a harsher death works for a lighter one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה 'כל חייבי מיתות' and infers that a person warned for a harsher death penalty can be punished with a lighter one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: all those liable to different death penalties who got mixed up are executed with the lightest one. Learn from this that someone warned for a severe punishment is considered warned for a lighter punishment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה and draws a rule from it about warnings (התראה).
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each condemned man was warned about his own specific death penalty. If the משנה lets a man who was warned about סקילה be killed with a lighter death, then the warning about the harsher death must also count for the lighter one.

keyTerms.meaning: People liable to death penalties from בית דין
Learn from it (a proof formula)
Someone who was given a warning (התראה)
A severe matter / a lighter matter

phrases.english: All those liable to death penalties...
phrases.notes: These are the opening words of the משנה, which rules that mixed-up condemned men get the lightest death.

phrases.english: learn from it
one who is warned for a severe matter –
is considered warned for a lighter matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of the condemned cow and returns to a new line of the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a warning for a harsher death counts for a lighter death
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה that mixed-up condemned men are given the lightest death penalty

steps.title: רבי ירמיה: the warning was general
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה rejects the proof. He says the משנה is talking about men who were warned only that they would be killed, without naming which death.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה said: What case are we dealing with here? One where they warned him in a general way.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה pushes back on the proof from step 3 by setting the משנה in a narrower case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the witnesses never named a specific death, no one was warned for a harsher death in particular. So giving the lighter death proves nothing about whether a harsher warning covers a lighter one.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow the case)
They warned him
Generally, without details

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya said:
With what are we dealing here?
For instance, where they warned him without specifying.
phrases.notes: They told him he would be put to death, but not which kind of death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of step 3 by limiting the משנה to a general warning.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof. It does not decide whether a harsher warning works for a lighter one.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed each man was warned about a specific death, but the משנה could be talking about a general warning.

steps.title: The משנה follows the תנא who does not require naming the death
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה shows his reading fits a known תנא. The ברייתא's first opinion requires only a warning that the person faces death from בית דין, while רבי יהודה requires naming the specific death.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this follows that תנא, as it is taught in a ברייתא: All the other people liable to death penalties in the Torah are executed only with a court, witnesses, and a warning, and only once they told him that he is liable to death from בית דין. רבי יהודה says: only once they told him by which death he will be killed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה supports his reading by showing that a general warning is enough according to the first opinion in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says the warning only has to mention a death penalty from בית דין, so a general warning works. רבי יהודה says the warning must name the exact death. So the משנה, as רבי ירמיה reads it, follows the תנא קמא and not רבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: And this follows that תנא (ties a ruling to a specific opinion)
Congregation, here meaning the court
A warning given before the sin
A death penalty carried out by the court

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה does not prove that a harsher warning covers a lighter death. According to רבי ירמיה, it is a case of a general warning, following the תנא קמא who does not require naming the specific death, unlike רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: And this is that tanna, as it is taught:
And the rest of those liable to death penalties in the Torah
phrases.notes: 'The rest' means everyone other than the מסית, the one who incites others to idol worship, whom this ברייתא discussed before.

phrases.english: they do not execute them except
with a congregation, witnesses, and a warning,
and only once they inform him
that he is liable to a court-imposed death.
Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: עַד שֶׁיּוֹדִיעוּהוּ בְּאֵיזֶה מִיתָה הוּא נֶהֱרָג.
phrases.english: only once they inform him by which death he is to be killed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up רבי ירמיה's rejection in step 4 by showing which תנא allows a general warning.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ירמיה's claim that a general warning is enough to execute
steps.raayaSupportSource: The תנא קמא of the ברייתא, who requires only telling the person he faces death from בית דין (as opposed to רבי יהודה)

steps.title: The root of the argument: the wood gatherer
steps.stepSummary: The first תנא learns the rules of warning from the מקושש. רבי יהודה says that case was a one-time ruling and cannot be used as a source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first תנא learns from the wood gatherer. רבי יהודה says the wood gatherer was a one-time ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the first תנא and רבי יהודה disagree about whether the warning must name the specific death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מקושש was put to death even though, at the time he was warned, no one knew which death he would get. So the first תנא proves that a general warning of 'you will be killed' is enough. רבי יהודה says that case was a special one-time ruling, so no lasting rule can be learned from it.

keyTerms.meaning: The man who gathered wood on שבת in the desert
Learns, derives
A one-time ruling for that moment only, not a rule for all generations
The first, unnamed opinion in a ברייתא or משנה

steps.whatToRemember: The first תנא says a general warning is enough, based on the מקושש. רבי יהודה says you must name the specific death, because the מקושש was a one-time case.

phrases.english: The first tanna learns from the wood gatherer,
phrases.notes: במדבר 15:32–36. He was warned without being told which death, since even משה did not know yet.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda says:
the wood gatherer was a one-time ruling.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the source behind each side of the ברייתא quoted in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first תנא's view comes from the מקושש. רבי יהודה rejects that source because it was a one-time ruling.

steps.title: רב יחזקאל's wording of the mixed-group case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of נסקלין mixed with נשרפין. Then it brings רב יחזקאל's version, which flips the order, with רבי שמעון saying they are all stoned because burning is harsher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those to be stoned mixed with those to be burned. רב יחזקאל taught his son רמי: those to be burned mixed with those to be stoned. רבי שמעון says they are judged with stoning, because burning is harsher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic: a group of condemned people where we no longer know who gets which death. This step sets up the wording that the next steps will argue about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב יחזקאל's version, a few people sentenced to burning got mixed into a bigger group sentenced to stoning. רבי שמעון rules that everyone gets stoning. His reason is that burning is the harsher death, so the lighter death of stoning can be given even to those who deserve burning.

keyTerms.meaning: People sentenced to סקילה (stoning)
People sentenced to שריפה (burning)
Taught, recited the wording
They shall be judged, sentenced
More severe, harsher

steps.confusionAlert: Pay attention to the order of the words. 'X among Y' means a few X's got mixed into a bigger group of Y's. So 'הנשרפין בנסקלין' means most of the group are to be stoned.

phrases.english: Those to be stoned [mixed] among those to be burned,

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַב יְחֶזְקֵאל לְרָמֵי בְּרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Yechezkel taught it to Rami his son:
Those to be burned among those to be stoned,
Rabbi Shimon says: they shall be judged with stoning,
for burning is more severe.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנֵי לֵיהּ רַב יְחֶזְקֵאל לְרָמֵי בְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה, not connected to the warning discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In רב יחזקאל's version, when people to be burned are mixed into people to be stoned, רבי שמעון says they are all stoned because burning is harsher.

steps.title: רב יהודה: with that wording, the majority already decides
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה tells his father not to teach it that way. If most of the group are to be stoned, the majority alone explains stoning, so there is no need for the 'burning is harsher' reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said to him: Father, don't teach it like that. Why give the reason that burning is harsher? You could get the same answer because most of them are to be stoned!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה challenges his father's wording. He says it makes רבי שמעון's reason pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a mixture, we normally follow the majority. In רב יחזקאל's version most of the group are to be stoned, so stoning everyone is obvious. Then רבי שמעון's special reason, 'burning is harsher', adds nothing, and that suggests the wording is wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't teach it this way
Why specifically this? Why pick this reason?
Derive it instead from…, there is a simpler reason
Majority

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said to him:
Father, do not teach it this way.
Why specifically because burning is more severe?
Derive it from the fact that most of them are to be stoned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording that רב יחזקאל taught in step 7.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If most of the group are to be stoned, following the majority already gives stoning. So רבי שמעון's 'burning is harsher' reason would be unnecessary.

steps.title: So how should it be taught?
steps.stepSummary: רב יחזקאל asks his son what the right wording would be.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, how should I teach it?
steps.whatsHappening: The father asks for another wording. This short line sets up רב יהודה's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רב יחזקאל accepts that the challenge has force, and asks his son to suggest a better wording.

keyTerms.meaning: How should I teach it?

phrases.english: Rather, how shall I teach it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Responds to the challenge by asking for another wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What is the correct wording of רבי שמעון's case?

steps.title: רב יהודה's wording: most of the group are burners
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says to teach 'הנסקלין בנשרפין', so most of the group are to be burned. Then רבי שמעון needs the 'burning is harsher' reason to explain why they are all stoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those to be stoned mixed among those to be burned. רבי שמעון says they are judged with stoning, because burning is harsher.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה gives his version of the wording. Now a few people to be stoned are mixed into a bigger group of people to be burned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the majority would point toward burning. Even so, רבי שמעון says to stone everyone, because stoning is the lighter death and it is included in burning. In this wording, his 'burning is harsher' reason is really needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Death by stoning
Death by burning

phrases.english: Those to be stoned among those to be burned,
Rabbi Shimon says: they shall be judged with stoning,
for burning is more severe.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַנִּסְקָלִין בַּנִּשְׂרָפִין רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר יִדּוֹנוּ בִּסְקִילָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 with a wording that solves the problem raised in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Teach it as 'הנסקלין בנשרפין': most of the group are to be burned, so רבי שמעון's severity reason is needed.

steps.title: The same problem now hits the Sages
steps.stepSummary: If most of the group are burners, then the חכמים's ruling of burning is already explained by the majority. So their reason, 'stoning is harsher', becomes unnecessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end of the משנה: The Sages say they are judged with burning, because stoning is harsher. You could get the same answer because most of them are to be burned!
steps.whatsHappening: The father pushes back on his son's wording. The same 'majority' problem now shows up in the second half of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה's wording fixed רבי שמעון's line, but it broke the חכמים's line. With most of the group being burners, the חכמים would not need to say 'stoning is harsher' to explain why everyone is burned. So neither wording seems to fit both halves of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, if your wording is right
Look at the end part of the משנה
The Sages, the majority opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic problem: changing the wording to save one opinion can create the same problem in the other opinion. The גמרא still has to find a reading that fits both.

phrases.english: If so, say the last clause:
and the Sages say: they shall be judged with burning,
for stoning is more severe.
Derive it from the fact that most of them are to be burned!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יהודה's new wording from step 10 by using the end of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With that wording, most of the group are to be burned, so the majority already gives burning. Then the חכמים's reason, 'stoning is harsher', would be unnecessary. This is the same problem רב יהודה raised against his father.

steps.title: The Rabbis are only answering רבי שמעון's argument
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the חכמים's line 'סקילה is harsher' is not their main reason. It is a reply to רבי שמעון's claim that שריפה is harsher.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, it is the Rabbis who are speaking to רבי שמעון: 'You say burning is harsher. No! Stoning is harsher.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question from Step 11. He says the חכמים's reason is a reply to רבי שמעון, not the real basis of their ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב יהודה's version, the חכמים burn everyone simply because most of the group are burners. רבי שמעון objected that burning is harsher, so you cannot give it to the stoning minority. The חכמים answer, 'No, סקילה is harsher,' so giving the minority burning only makes it easier for them, and following the majority works.

keyTerms.meaning: There. Here it points to the end part (סיפא) of the משנה, where the חכמים speak.
The Rabbis, meaning the חכמים who argue with רבי שמעון
According to you, on your own view

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the חכמים burn everyone because 'סקילה is harsher.' They burn everyone because most of the group are burners. The 'harsher' line only answers רבי שמעון's objection.

phrases.english: There, it is the Rabbis who are saying
phrases.notes: 'There' means the end part of the משנה, where the חכמים give their reason.

phrases.english: to Rabbi Shimon:
According to you, who say burning is more severe,
No! Stoning is more severe.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם, רַבָּנַן הוּא דְּקָאָמְרוּ לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the objection in Step 11 against רב יהודה's version.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframes the statement: the חכמים's reason is a reply to רבי שמעון, not their own main reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חכמים's reason 'סקילה is harsher' is wasted, because the majority already explains why they burn everyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: The majority is the real reason. 'סקילה is harsher' only removes רבי שמעון's objection, since burning the minority gives them a lighter death.

steps.title: שמואל addresses רב יהודה with a nickname
steps.stepSummary: שמואל begins speaking to רב יהודה and calls him 'שיננא'. This opens his reaction to the exchange.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said to רב יהודה: 'Long-toothed one,'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. שמואל calls out to רב יהודה, and what he has to say about this exchange continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On this amud we only see how שמואל addresses רב יהודה. The actual content of his statement comes on the next amud. This line just marks that a new speaker is joining the discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Long-toothed one', a nickname שמואל used for his sharp student רב יהודה

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה: שִׁינָּנָא,
phrases.english: Shmuel said to Rav Yehuda: Long-toothed one,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לְרַב יְהוּדָה: שִׁינָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב יהודה finishes defending his version, his teacher שמואל begins to respond to him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No ruling yet. This line only introduces שמואל's coming statement to רב יהודה.
